projects.name: Analytics Dashboard Platform
projects.description:
A new analytics dashboard platform that ingests customer CSV files and application logs, processes them into a unified analytics model, and serves interactive visualizations.

Scope:
- CSV ingestion and validation for customer data exports
- Application log parsing, normalization, and aggregation
- Data modeling / warehouse layer for blended metrics
- Visualization component library and dashboard composition
- Integration, testing, and deployment

Structure: 6 major milestones, each decomposed into executable tasks sized for a single work session (complexity <= 6/10).

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-pipeline, csv, log-analysis, visualization

tasks.name: M1: Project Foundation & Data Architecture
tasks.details:
MILESTONE 1 of 6. Establish the skeleton of the platform before any pipeline work begins: repo structure, tooling, environment config, and the agreed data contract for customer CSV and log sources.

Exit criteria:
- Repository scaffolded with CI running lint + tests
- Local dev environment reproducible from a single command
- Written data contract covering both CSV and log source schemas
- Technology decisions recorded in an ADR

All execution work lives in the child tasks; this milestone tracks completion only.

tasks.name: M2: Customer CSV Ingestion Pipeline
tasks.details:
MILESTONE 2 of 6. Build a reliable ingestion path for customer CSV files: discovery, parsing, schema validation, cleaning, deduplication, and landing into staging storage.

Exit criteria:
- CSV files validated against the data contract with actionable error reports
- Malformed rows quarantined rather than silently dropped
- Deduplicated, typed records landed in staging tables
- Backfill of a historical file set completes end-to-end

All execution work lives in the child tasks; this milestone tracks completion only.

tasks.name: M3: Application Log Analysis Pipeline
tasks.details:
MILESTONE 3 of 6. Turn raw application logs into structured, queryable event data: parsing, normalization, PII scrubbing, enrichment, and metric aggregation.

Exit criteria:
- All supported log formats parsed with per-format coverage measured
- Sensitive fields redacted before persistence
- Normalized events queryable with service/severity/time dimensions
- Hourly and daily aggregates produced for error rate, latency, and volume

All execution work lives in the child tasks; this milestone tracks completion only.

tasks.name: M4: Data Modeling & Metrics Layer
tasks.details:
MILESTONE 4 of 6. Unify customer and log data into a dimensional model and define the reusable metrics layer that every visualization consumes.

Exit criteria:
- Star schema (facts + dimensions) documented and implemented
- Customer-to-log correlation key resolved and tested
- Metric definitions version-controlled and unit tested against known fixtures
- Data quality checks run on every model refresh

All execution work lives in the child tasks; this milestone tracks completion only.

tasks.name: M5: Visualization Components & Dashboards
tasks.details:
MILESTONE 5 of 6. Build the charting foundation and compose the actual dashboards on top of the metrics layer.

Exit criteria:
- Reusable chart components with consistent theming and loading/empty/error states
- Query layer wired to the metrics API with caching
- Customer analytics dashboard + application health dashboard shipped
- Accessibility and responsive layout verified

All execution work lives in the child tasks; this milestone tracks completion only.

tasks.name: M6: Integration, Testing & Launch Readiness
tasks.details:
MILESTONE 6 of 6. Prove the whole chain works together and make it operable: end-to-end tests, performance validation, observability, docs, and rollout.

Exit criteria:
- End-to-end test runs CSV + logs through to rendered dashboard in CI
- Performance validated at target volume with documented limits
- Monitoring, alerting, and runbooks in place
- Production deploy executed with rollback plan

All execution work lives in the child tasks; this milestone tracks completion only.

tasks.name: Scaffold monorepo and CI pipeline
tasks.details:
Create the repository skeleton and automated checks.

Steps:
1. Init repo with folders: /ingestion, /pipelines, /models, /api, /web, /infra, /docs
2. Add .gitignore, editorconfig, and formatting config
3. Add CI workflow: install -> lint -> unit tests -> build, triggered on PR
4. Add branch protection notes and PR template
5. Commit a trivial smoke test so CI is green on day one

Done when: a PR runs lint + tests automatically and passes.

tasks.name: Set up local development environment
tasks.details:
Make the whole stack runnable locally with one command.

Steps:
1. Write docker-compose with database, queue, and app services
2. Add .env.example with every required variable documented
3. Add a seed script with a small anonymized CSV + sample log file
4. Write `make dev` (or equivalent) that boots everything
5. Verify a fresh clone reaches a running state following only the README

Done when: a clean clone boots in under 10 minutes from the README alone.

tasks.name: Document source data contract for CSV and log inputs
tasks.details:
Write the single source of truth for what we ingest.

Steps:
1. Collect 3 real (or sanitized) sample CSV exports and 3 sample log files
2. Tabulate CSV columns: name, type, nullability, example, business meaning, owner
3. Tabulate each log format with field paths, timestamp format, and severity mapping
4. Record known data quality issues found in the samples (bad dates, dupes, encoding)
5. Define the canonical internal field names both sources map into
6. Get sign-off from the data owner

Done when: /docs/data-contract.md is reviewed and no source field is unexplained.

tasks.name: Write ADR for core technology choices
tasks.details:
A short decision record so the team does not relitigate the stack later.

Cover, with a one-paragraph rationale each:
1. Processing engine (e.g. Python + Polars/Pandas vs. SQL-based)
2. Storage/warehouse choice and why it fits our volume
3. Orchestration approach (scheduler vs. cron vs. queue workers)
4. Frontend charting library
5. Hosting target

Include the alternatives considered and the specific constraint that ruled each out. Keep it under 2 pages.

Done when: ADR merged and one reviewer has signed off.

tasks.name: Build CSV file discovery and intake manifest
tasks.details:
Know exactly which files exist, when they arrived, and whether they were processed.

Steps:
1. Define the intake folder convention and the drop-off locations we watch
2. Compute file fingerprint (name + size + hash) to detect re-drops
3. Persist an intake manifest table: file id, source, checksum, status, row count, ingested_at
4. Implement idempotent "skip if already processed" logic keyed on checksum
5. Log a structured event per file at start and finish

Done when: dropping the same file twice processes it once and both events are visible.

tasks.name: Implement CSV parser with schema validation
tasks.details:
Read CSVs into typed records and reject anything that violates the data contract.

Steps:
1. Configure the reader for encoding detection, delimiter, quoting, and header handling
2. Encode the data contract as an executable schema (types + required fields)
3. Validate every row; collect a validation error object per failing row
4. Handle type coercion explicitly: dates, decimals, currency, booleans, empty->null
5. Emit a per-file validation summary: total rows, valid, invalid, per-column error counts
6. Unit test with fixtures covering BOM, CRLF, quoted commas, and ragged rows

Done when: a deliberately corrupted 1,000-row fixture yields exactly the expected invalid count.

tasks.name: Implement row cleaning and normalization rules
tasks.details:
Turn messy-but-valid values into consistent canonical values.

Rules to implement (one test each):
1. Trim and collapse whitespace in string fields
2. Normalize whitespace in and case of email addresses
3. Normalize country codes and region names to a controlled list
4. Parse and standardize all dates to UTC ISO-8601
5. Split or map free-text plan/tier values to a canonical set
6. Unify phone number and other identifier formats
7. Publish a rule table documenting input -> output for every transformation

Done when: normalization is deterministic and every rule has a passing fixture test.

tasks.name: Build quarantine store and error reporting
tasks.details:
No row should vanish silently. Invalid rows get preserved and explained.

Steps:
1. Create a quarantine table: raw row payload, source file, row number, failure reasons
2. Route schema-invalid rows to quarantine instead of dropping them
3. Emit a human-readable error report per run grouped by failure reason
4. Add a re-process command that replays quarantined rows after a fix
5. Alert when the invalid-row rate for a file exceeds a configurable threshold

Done when: a 100-row file with 10 bad rows lands 90 clean + 10 quarantined, all accounted for.

tasks.name: Add deduplication and load clean records to staging
tasks.details:
Guarantee one authoritative record per customer.

Steps:
1. Choose the business key that defines a unique customer record
2. Resolve conflicts when the same key appears with differing values (latest-wins with a documented tiebreak)
3. Upsert into staging tables using merge semantics, not blind insert
4. Make the whole load idempotent so a rerun produces identical row counts
5. Report rows inserted vs. updated vs. unchanged per run

Done when: running the same batch twice leaves staging unchanged on the second pass.

tasks.name: Run historical CSV backfill and reconcile counts
tasks.details:
Prove the pipeline handles the real historical file set.

Steps:
1. Inventory all historical files and their date ranges
2. Run the pipeline over the full set in chronological order
3. Reconcile: source row count == staged + quarantined, per file, with zero tolerance
4. Investigate and document every reconciliation gap
5. Record total runtime and cost for the backfill in the docs

Done when: every historical file reconciles to zero unexplained rows and the numbers are recorded.

tasks.name: Inventory log formats and build sample corpus
tasks.details:
You cannot parse what you have not catalogued.

Steps:
1. Enumerate every service and log source we must support
2. For each, capture 200+ representative lines including rare and error cases
3. Classify each format: JSON structured, key=value, plain text, multi-line stack traces
4. Record sampling stats: lines/day, avg line size, peak burst rate
5. Note formats that must be explicitly out of scope for v1

Done when: /docs/log-formats.md lists every in-scope format with a sample file attached.

tasks.name: Build structured JSON log parser
tasks.details:
Handle the JSON/formatted log sources from the inventory.

Steps:
1. Parse line-delimited JSON safely, tolerating truncated or interleaved lines
2. Map nested field paths to canonical internal names from the data contract
3. Preserve unknown fields in a raw/metadata bag so nothing is lost
4. Handle multi-line entries (stack traces) via a continuation-line rule
5. Count and report parse failures per file rather than aborting the batch
6. Fixture tests per format with expected field-by-field output

Done when: every JSON format in the inventory parses at >99.9% of lines in its sample corpus.

tasks.name: Build plain-text log pattern library and parser
tasks.details:
Cover the unstructured formats with a maintainable pattern set.

Steps:
1. Define a versioned pattern library (one named regex per format) in config, not code
2. Extract timestamp, level, service, message, and request id per pattern
3. Add a fallback pattern so unmatched lines still land with raw message retained
4. Require each pattern to declare which named groups it guarantees
5. Build a coverage report: lines matched per pattern vs. fallback
6. Test each pattern against its sample corpus and a set of near-miss negatives

Done when: fallback rate is under 1% on the full sample corpus and each pattern has tests.

tasks.name: Normalize timestamps, severity levels, and service names
tasks.details:
Parsed does not mean comparable. Make every event align on shared dimensions.

Steps:
1. Infer the source timezone per service and convert all timestamps to UTC
2. Detect and repair obviously wrong timestamps (epoch seconds vs. ms, clock skew > threshold)
3. Map each source's severity vocabulary to a canonical scale: DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR/FATAL
4. Canonicalize service names (handles env suffixes, replicas, legacy names)
5. Document every mapping in a lookup table committed to the repo
6. Test with deliberately ambiguous and out-of-range timestamps

Done when: a mixed-format sample yields 100% of events with valid UTC time, canonical severity, and known service.

tasks.name: Implement PII redaction and retention guards
tasks.details:
Logs leak customer data by accident. Redact before persistence, not after.

Steps:
1. Enumerate sensitive patterns: emails, phone numbers, tokens/API keys, card numbers, IPs (per policy), internal hostnames
2. Implement masking rules that preserve usefulness (e.g. j***@example.com, last-4 only)
3. Apply redaction immediately after parsing, before any write to storage
4. Add a retention policy: TTL or partition-drop for events older than the agreed window
5. Add a pre-commit/CI scan that fails on new unmasked patterns in fixtures
6. Test that redacted values are unrecoverable from stored records

Done when: a fixture seeded with 20 known PII values yields zero recoverable values in storage.

tasks.name: Build log aggregation jobs for volume, error rate, and latency
tasks.details:
Turn event rows into the numbers the dashboard actually charts.

Steps:
1. Define grain: hourly and daily buckets by service and severity
2. Implement volume counts (event count, distinct requests)
3. Implement error rate as errors / total per bucket, with a defined denominator
4. Extract latency from structured fields and compute p50/p95/p99 per bucket
5. Handle late-arriving events with a lookback window and recomputation rule
6. Backfill 30 days of aggregates and compare against a manual spot-check query

Done when: aggregates for 3 sampled hours match hand-computed values exactly.

tasks.name: Design and document the star schema
tasks.details:
Design first, build second. This is a paper + diagram task.

Steps:
1. Identify the business processes being measured (customer activity, service health)
2. Declare grain for each fact table in one sentence
3. List dimensions: customer, date, service, severity, geography
4. For each dimension, define attributes, SCD handling (type 1 vs type 2), and natural key
5. Draw the schema diagram and commit it to /docs
6. Walk it through with one consumer (dashboard owner) to confirm it answers real questions

Done when: the diagram + grain statements are reviewed and each dashboard question maps to a column.

tasks.name: Resolve customer-to-log correlation key
tasks.details:
Joining customers to their application events is the riskiest step. Prove it works.

Steps:
1. Determine what identifier, if any, links a log event to a customer (account id, email, tenant)
2. Quantify match rate against a real day of logs and a real CSV export
3. Define fallback matching (email normalization, hashed id) where the direct key is missing
4. Handle many-to-one and one-to-many cases explicitly; no accidental fan-out in joins
5. Build an identity mapping table with confidence/source columns
6. Report: % of events attributed to a customer, % unattributed (unattributed must be a visible dashboard number, not hidden)

Done when: match rate is measured on real data and join fan-out is proven absent by a row-count test.

tasks.name: Implement fact and dimension tables
tasks.details:
Build the approved design as repeatable table definitions.

Steps:
1. Create dimension tables with surrogate keys and natural key uniqueness constraints
2. Create fact tables at the declared grain with foreign keys to each dimension
3. Implement SCD type 2 history on the customer dimension
4. Build the refresh process as full-rebuild-first, incremental later
5. Add referential integrity tests: no orphan facts, no duplicate dimension keys
6. Verify each fact table row count matches its source aggregate within tolerance

Done when: all tables build from scratch on a clean database and integrity tests pass.

tasks.name: Build versioned metrics definition layer
tasks.details:
One definition of "active customer" or "error rate" for the whole platform.

Steps:
1. Collect the metric list from the dashboard requirements (target ~8-12 metrics)
2. For each metric write: name, plain-English definition, formula, grain, filters, owner
3. Implement metrics as version-controlled config/SQL, not hardcoded in the frontend
4. Add unit tests that run each metric against a small fixture with hand-checked expected values
5. Expose metrics through a single query interface the API will use
6. Document deprecation rules for changing a metric definition

Done when: every metric has a test with a known-correct expected number and no metric logic lives in the UI.

tasks.name: Add data quality checks to model refresh
tasks.details:
Catch bad data before it reaches a chart someone trusts.

Checks to implement (each as a failing test, not a silent log line):
1. Freshness: data is no older than N hours
2. Volume: row counts within expected range of trailing average
3. Uniqueness: no duplicate primary keys in dimensions
4. Referential integrity: zero orphaned fact rows
5. Null rate: critical columns under threshold
6. Range: no negative counts, no future-dated events

Steps: wire checks to run after each refresh, block promotion on failure, and surface results in a simple status view.

Done when: deliberately breaking the data causes the refresh to fail loudly with a specific reason.

tasks.name: Create design system and chart component shell
tasks.details:
Every chart shares a wrapper, so build the wrapper once.

Steps:
1. Define design tokens: color palette, typography scale, spacing, chart color series
2. Build a <ChartCard> shell handling title, subtitle, filters, and actions
3. Implement the four required states: loading skeleton, empty, error with retry, and loaded
4. Define a shared tooltip and legend component
5. Publish a Storybook (or equivalent) page with every state visible
6. Add a chart color palette that is colorblind-safe

Done when: a placeholder chart renders all four states in the component gallery.

tasks.name: Implement core chart components
tasks.details:
Build the small set of chart types the dashboards actually need. Resist adding more.

Components:
1. Time-series line chart (multi-series, with date-range zoom)
2. Stacked bar chart (severity breakdown)
3. Single-value KPI tile with trend delta and sparkline
4. Horizontal bar ranking chart (top services by error count)
5. Data table with sorting and pagination for drill-down

Steps: one component per PR, typed props, unit tests for data transforms, and a docs entry with a usage example.

Done when: all five components render from fixture data in the gallery with no console errors.

tasks.name: Build metrics API client with caching
tasks.details:
The browser should never talk to the warehouse directly.

Steps:
1. Wrap each metric in a REST/GraphQL endpoint with explicit date-range and filter params
2. Validate and clamp inputs server-side (max range, allowed groupings)
3. Add response caching keyed on metric + params with a short TTL
4. Implement a typed client in the frontend with request cancellation on filter change
5. Standardize error envelopes so the UI can show real messages
6. Add request-level timing logs to find slow metrics

Done when: a dashboard loads from cache on repeat visit and a bad parameter returns a clear 4xx, not a 500.

tasks.name: Compose customer analytics dashboard
tasks.details:
Assemble the customer-facing view from existing components and metrics.

Steps:
1. Lay out sections: KPI header row, activity trend, segment breakdown, top accounts table
2. Wire a global date-range and segment filter that all tiles respect
3. Ensure every tile shows its metric definition on hover (no mystery numbers)
4. Handle the no-data case for new segments gracefully
5. Add a shareable URL that encodes current filters
6. Review with one business stakeholder and capture feedback as follow-up tasks

Done when: a stakeholder can answer their top 3 questions without asking an engineer.

tasks.name: Compose application health dashboard
tasks.details:
The operational view built on the log aggregates.

Steps:
1. Lay out sections: error-rate KPI, volume trend, severity breakdown, latency percentiles, top failing services
2. Add a service selector that filters the whole page
3. Show data freshness explicitly (last updated timestamp + stale warning)
4. Link each failing service row to its filtered event drill-down
5. Add a simple threshold indicator (green/amber/red) driven by config, not hardcoded
6. Validate against a known incident window and confirm the chart reflects it

Done when: replaying a past incident shows the error spike at the correct time on the chart.

tasks.name: Run accessibility and responsive verification
tasks.details:
Make the dashboards usable, not just pretty.

Steps:
1. Keyboard-navigate every interactive element; fix focus traps and missing focus rings
2. Add ARIA labels and table-alternative summaries for each chart
3. Verify contrast ratios meet WCAG AA for text and chart series
4. Test layout at 1280px, 1024px, and 768px widths; fix overflow and squashed charts
5. Run an automated axe (or equivalent) scan across all dashboard routes
6. Record remaining known issues in a short accessibility notes file

Done when: automated scan reports zero critical issues and all three breakpoints render without overflow.

tasks.name: Build end-to-end test harness in CI
tasks.details:
One test that proves the whole chain works: CSV + logs -> models -> metrics -> API -> rendered dashboard.

Steps:
1. Create a small deterministic dataset (CSV + logs) with known expected metrics
2. Script the run: ingest, transform, aggregate, build model, serve API
3. Assert the API returns the hand-computed expected values
4. Add a smoke test that loads each dashboard route headlessly and checks tiles render
5. Run it in CI on every PR with a reasonable timeout
6. Publish failure artifacts (logs + screenshots) for debugging

Done when: breaking any stage's output makes the E2E job fail with a message naming the stage.

tasks.name: Run performance benchmark at target volume
tasks.details:
Find the breaking point before users do.

Steps:
1. Agree target numbers: rows per CSV load, log events per day, dashboard load time
2. Generate synthetic data at 1x and 3x target volume
3. Measure each stage: ingest time, transform time, model build, API p95 latency
4. Identify the first bottleneck and record the contributing factor (memory, IO, query plan)
5. Optimize the single worst bottleneck only; re-measure
6. Document throughput and the volume at which we expect to need a redesign

Done when: a written benchmark table exists and dashboard p95 load meets the agreed target at 1x volume.

tasks.name: Set up monitoring, alerting, and pipeline SLIs
tasks.details:
If a pipeline silently stops, the dashboards lie. Detect it fast.

Steps:
1. Define SLIs: freshness (age of newest data), success rate per job, duration, rows processed
2. Emit metrics from each pipeline stage with run id and source
3. Build 3-4 alerts: job failed, job overdue, freshness breached, invalid-row rate high
4. Route alerts to the on-call channel and verify a test alert arrives
5. Add a simple pipeline status page showing last run per source
6. Set thresholds from the benchmark baseline, not guesses

Done when: stopping a job for longer than its SLA triggers exactly one actionable alert.

tasks.name: Write operator runbooks and data dictionary
tasks.details:
Whoever is on call at 2am has never seen this system. Write for them.

Runbooks:
1. A failing CSV ingest: how to inspect the quarantine, decide reprocess vs. fix upstream
2. A log parser regression: how to roll back a pattern version
3. Stale data on the dashboard: triage order from source to chart
4. How to trigger a manual backfill and estimate its cost

Plus a data dictionary: every table, column, metric with a plain-English definition and owner.

Done when: someone not on the project can follow a runbook end-to-end and resolve a simulated failure.

tasks.name: Deploy to production and rehearse rollback
tasks.details:
Ship it, but know how to un-ship it.

Steps:
1. Define environments (staging, prod) and promote the same artifact to each
2. Provision production infrastructure as code, reviewed before apply
3. Run the full pipeline once in prod against a limited data window
4. Execute a rollback drill: revert to previous version, confirm dashboards still serve
5. Announce the launch with a short internal note (what it does, known limits)
6. Schedule a 1-week check-in to review usage and data quality

Done when: production serves both dashboards from real data and a rollback completes in under 15 minutes.
